exact_statement: Under Faul-Hoessly-Xia's equal-source-set, complete-graph, strictly-positive-rate Langevin interface, networks are confoundable iff the strict positive lifted-signature cones intersect at every source; therefore they are unconfoundable iff at least one common source has disjoint cones. Different source sets also preclude generator equality.
assumptions: mass-action Langevin approximation
complete candidate reaction graphs and known species set
all rates strictly positive
structural generator/law comparison over a positive open state set
source complexes index distinct monomials
status: internally reconstructed correction to a published theorem statement; witness exact-check passed; external confirmation and independent review absent
novelty_boundary: Logical quantifier correction, not a scientific priority claim; published Theorem 5.15 and §7.3 proof support the all-source intersection criterion for confoundability, while Theorem 3.3(2) states an incorrect universal disjointness criterion.
costs: No data acquisition; exact coefficient algebra and one bounded integer/rational witness; proof review and author/editor inquiry still needed.
falsifier: A strictly-positive generator-equality witness for the two one-species networks in observability_correction.md, or an erratum/author derivation establishing a different definition of the cones or confoundability.
next_gate: Independent mathematical review against the published theorem definitions and proof; then request author/editor confirmation.

exact_statement: The two E:S4 release networks with rate vectors (1,1,4,0) and (0,4,1,1) have identical mass-action ODE drift, identical full Langevin covariance, and identical Exp(6) first-event times, but differ in their exact endpoint product-yield law. Five independent completed turnovers and an exact LR test give combined type-I-plus-type-II error 181/3888 < 0.05; four cannot reach that threshold.
assumptions: one correctly prepared E:S4 intermediate per assay
four yields k=1..4 with stoichiometry C to E+(4-k)S+kP
fixed candidate rate vectors and independent assays
integer product-yield measurement with negligible error, or a calibrated confusion matrix
no background reactions or hidden pathways
right censoring is distinguished from zero product
status: conditional finite CTMC construction; exact rational likelihood calculation and moment audit pass; real chemical instantiation and novelty unknown
novelty_boundary: Constructive application of the second-order lifted-signature obstruction to a finite partial-output CTMC assay; no general noisy partial-observation theorem, real-enzyme result, or priority claim.
costs: Five preformed intermediates and five product-yield readings; assay deadline T>=log(500)/6 gives <=1% batch-censoring union bound; estimated parallel completion maximum H5/6=137/360 time units. Preparation, purification, assay calibration, readout precision, and background costs are not priced.
falsifier: Both yield-1 and yield-4 outcomes in one batch, which has probability zero under either candidate, or a calibrated yield-frequency goodness-of-fit rejection of both fixed multinomial laws.
next_gate: Find a chemically plausible substrate/intermediate realizing the four channels; calibrate yield misclassification/background, then preregister a matched multinomial power test.

exact_statement: For a stationary resolved autonomous N-state unicycle with positive forward/reverse rates, cycle affinity A=sum_i log(k_i^+/k_i^-), and bare rate-parameter sum K=sum_i(k_i^++k_i^-), |J| <= (K/N^2) tanh(|A|/(2N)); the uniform stationary ring attains equality. Under K<=Kmax the inverse yields |A|>=2N artanh(N^2|J|/Kmax), with the stated LDB dissipation consequence only under complete reservoir accounting.
assumptions: autonomous finite CTMC unicycle with separate forward/backward channels
positive rates and stationary distribution
K is the sum of bare rate constants, not stationary jump traffic
thermodynamic interpretation requires local detailed balance and all reservoirs
status: internally reconstructed candidate theorem; finite seeded checks pass; priority unknown
novelty_boundary: N=3 bare-rate frontier is source-reported by Mottes et al.; general-N traffic-bound ETP is established by Yang-Dill. Arbitrary-N bare-rate sum extension may be a direct proof refinement; novelty not established. Does not apply to driven pumps without external-work accounting.
costs: Requires rate constants on each directed edge and a cycle-affinity/reservoir ledger; numerical fixture samples are finite diagnostics only.
falsifier: A positive-rate unicycle violating the inequality under the stated K definition, or a proof audit finding an invalid inequality step in PROOF.md.
next_gate: Independent proof audit, source-version/published-paper confirmation, and comparison with all prior bare-rate-budget formulations.

exact_statement: The remaining track-level statements are conditional model results: symmetry-erasing representations cannot recover signed mirror selectivity; shared multiplicative replicator drive preserves composition ratios; near-integer orbital occupations alone cannot certify a barrier error; untimed paths cannot identify absolute reaction rates under uniform rate scaling; and electrochemical selectivity/overpotential/turnover tradeoffs require explicit kinetic, transport, and cell assumptions.
assumptions: Each lane's own report interface and stated assumptions
no transfer of one track's theorem to another chemistry/model
source-reported evidence is not treated as experimental validation
status: individual conditional derivations and primary-source reconstructions completed; novelty generally unverified; no experiments run
novelty_boundary: These are separate scoped results and principal boundaries, not a combined general catalytic theorem.
costs: Track-specific acquisition and experimental costs are stated in each linked report; no wet-lab work was performed.
falsifier: A violation of the corresponding report's equations under its stated assumptions; chemistry-specific falsifiers are recorded in each report.
next_gate: Select a chemically validated system and perform the particular discriminating assay/model comparison in its track report.

exact_statement: For mirror catalysts c and tau(c) in a fixed achiral environment, if signed selectivity obeys y(tau(c))=-y(c) but a representation satisfies phi(tau(c))=phi(c), every predictor based only on phi has balanced-pair sign accuracy at most 1/2 and mean squared error at least y(c)^2. A stereochemical orientation bit distinguishes the pair but does not predict selectivity magnitude.
assumptions: signed target such as log(k_R/k_S) or signed ee
parity symmetry exchanges product labels
fixed achiral environment and conditions
representation is exactly invariant across the mirror pair
status: conditional theorem proved internally; experimental symmetry and model applicability not validated; novelty not claimed
novelty_boundary: General chirality-aware signed-selectivity modeling is established; this is an information-interface lower bound and test design, not a catalyst discovery.
costs: A paired assay needs verified enantiopurity, identical substrate/condition batches, replicate product and signed ee readout; synthesis and chiral chromatography are not priced.
falsifier: With verified mirror catalysts in a genuinely achiral fixed environment, a reproducible failure of the signed response to reverse beyond assay uncertainty challenges the physical symmetry assumptions; a stereo-blind model giving distinct predictions from identical representations contradicts its interface definition.
next_gate: Run a blinded, randomized, replicated matched-enantiomer assay and compare stereo-blind and stereo-aware models on held-out pairs/scaffolds.

exact_statement: For a finite Hermitian block Hamiltonian H=[[A,B],[B†,C]], e=lambda_min(A), C>=(e+gamma)I with gamma>0, and beta>=||B||_2, the retained-space ground-energy lowering is bounded sharply by 0<=e-lambda_min(H)<=(sqrt(gamma^2+4 beta^2)-gamma)/2<=beta^2/gamma. For two states, the error in their energy difference is bounded by the maximum of the two state-specific lowering bounds. Fixed discarded occupation alone does not bound energy error without a scale/gap/coupling bound.
assumptions: finite-dimensional Hermitian Hamiltonian
positive certified discarded-block gap gamma relative to retained ground energy
certified operator-norm coupling upper bound beta
retained variational ground energies are exact or separately budgeted
status: conditional finite-dimensional lemma proved internally; exact two-block counterexample and arithmetic fixture recorded; molecular integral bounds not obtained
novelty_boundary: The block-matrix bound is a standard variational/complement-space result and no priority claim is made; the 2026 Ru source reports endpoint energies, not a transition-state barrier or physical spin ground state.
costs: Requires molecular integrals and certified gap/coupling estimates for each geometry; the source compares classical CASCI spaces and does not report shot counts or device energy.
falsifier: A finite Hermitian block example satisfying the stated gamma/beta assumptions but violating the bound, or a computational fixture contradicting the exact block eigenvalue formula.
next_gate: Independently reproduce CASCI energies, then establish useful gamma and beta bounds along an actual transition-state path and compare against larger-space controls.

exact_statement: For positive absolutely continuous states satisfying dx_i/dt=(a_i u(t)-d_i(t))x_i+r_i(t), their log-ratio change is (a_i-a_j) integral u minus integral(d_i-d_j) plus integral(r_i/x_i-r_j/x_j); its deviation from the first two terms is bounded by integral(|r_i|/x_i+|r_j|/x_j). Equal efficiencies, equal losses, and zero residual flux preserve x_i/x_j. In the finite mass-action batch S+X->2X and S+Y->2Y with equal rate constants and initial (S,X,Y)=(100,9,1), total replicator amount grows 11-fold while the ratio remains 9:1.
assumptions: positive states on the interval
common nonnegative measurable exposure with finite integral
integrable species losses and residual ratios
deterministic model; stochastic finite-copy drift is not covered
fixture additionally assumes equal irreversible mass-action rates and complete substrate conversion
status: exact model identity and finite fixture checked internally; no experiment or novelty search; source-reported CaM/foldamer work is not a validation of this reduction
novelty_boundary: Log-derivative identity is elementary; the report applies it as a falsification boundary, not as a new general autocatalysis theorem.
costs: A discriminating assay needs species-resolved time courses, catalyst occupancy/exposure, loss rates, and non-autocatalytic source flux under matched competitor conditions; no wet-lab data were collected.
falsifier: After correcting for differential efficiency, loss, residual source flux, occupancy, and measurement error, a reproducible composition shift outside the residual bound rejects the shared scalar-field model.
next_gate: Run the matched two-template time-course assay with independently calibrated exposure, loss, and source controls.

exact_statement: For any pure-jump CTMC generator Q and c>0, the embedded jump-chain path law and success committors are invariant under Q->cQ, while all physical holding times are divided by c and physical transition frequencies multiplied by c. Thus untimed successful state sequences alone cannot identify an absolute transition rate or, absent an independently known prefactor, an absolute activation barrier.
assumptions: observations retain only state sequence and success conditioning
physical holding times, flux, and rate-scale calibration are absent
all transition rates are uniformly rescaled by the same positive constant
status: conditional identifiability theorem proved in report and exact finite-state witness reproduced; novelty unverified
novelty_boundary: Uniform time-rescaling is a standard path-law identifiability obstruction; this is an audit condition for absolute-rate claims, not a new rare-event sampler.
costs: To recover an absolute rate, acquire physical-time flux/holding-time measurements or independent rate-scale calibration; FFS additionally pays for interface trials, path memory, and physical-time flux.
falsifier: An untimed path statistic that changes under Q->cQ while maintaining the same embedded transition law, or an absolute rate inferred without any additional scale information.
next_gate: Benchmark path-only claims against a clocked flux and rate-scale control, charging trajectory evaluations and wall time.

exact_statement: There is no universal monotone relation between Faradaic product selectivity and local overpotential across catalysts: in the stated two-pathway steady model, equal Tafel exponents and equal reactant orders make the FE odds independent of eta and common surface concentration. With first-order kinetics coupled to a planar mass-transfer layer, j=j_lim k/(k_m+k) and the apparent Tafel slope is the ideal kinetic slope divided by 1-j/j_lim. Whole-cell stack energy per mole has the separate identity w_i=n_i F V_cell/FE_i, excluding auxiliaries.
assumptions: steady two-product currents account for all Faradaic charge and share a measured surface reactant concentration
Tafel/power-law rate forms and constant mass-transfer coefficient for the conditional transport equation
stack-energy identity uses full-cell voltage and measured product FE over the same interval
auxiliary, separation, feed, heat and pumping costs are excluded unless explicitly added
status: conditional kinetic counterexample and accounting identities derived internally; primary literature reviewed selectively; no electrochemical experiment performed
novelty_boundary: No universal FE-overpotential law is rejected by a counterexample; transport and full-cell equations are standard conditional models, not a new electrochemical performance law.
costs: A sector-resolved cell test needs local potential, flow, pH/CO2, product FE, full-cell voltage, catalyst matching, and carbon/charge balance; whole-system auxiliaries must be separately metered.
falsifier: The displayed equal-exponent/equal-order model does not falsify a universal law if its premises fail; a real application requires a matched segmented-cell intervention and full charge/material balance.
next_gate: Run a segmented-cell geometry/flow intervention with local potential and product-resolved FE, then add measured auxiliary power to the energy comparison.
